---
title: "Getting Started"
---

Before a student can get underway with a project, there are a few pieces of prerequisite knowledge that are recommended to prevent roadblocks further down the line.

* R and R Studio: The first couple weeks of class will ensure that you are set up with this software, as it is required for classwork. The guides on this website are written with R users in mind.
* Popular R packages: These packages will make appearances in some of the example projects on this site and greatly simplify the work of data analysis and visualization.
    <!-- Turn this into a table instead? -->
  * dplyr:
    * Click [here](dplyr-guide.qmd) to read a helpful guide written for STAT 3125 students like you.
    * Click [here](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/) to learn more from its official website.
  * finalfit:
    * Click [here](finalfit-guide.qmd) to read a helpful guide written for STAT 3125 students like you.
    * Click [here](https://finalfit.org/) to learn more from its official website.
  * ggplot2: 
    * Click [here](ggplot2-guide.qmd) to read a helpful guide written for STAT 3125 students like you.
    * Click [here](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) to learn more from its official website.

1. [Finding and Choosing a Dataset](finding-your-dataset.qmd)
2. [Choosing Your Research Question](choosing-your-question.qmd)
3. [Performing Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)](performing-eda.qmd)
4. Modeling Data (Working title)
5. Analyzing Results
6. Creating Your Report/Presentation
